facts.fact: The CENI's new electoral roll registration, open until 24 November 2026, is done at the fokontany on presentation of a national identity card, according to the 2424.mg report.
The Transition government's PMO/PGE-R programme says the Government will continue the digitalisation of the electoral roll and of the election process, including digital security of the roll.

note: A roll rebuild with 7,163,714 provisional registrants is reported, but the roll is not said to be digital or biometric, nor checked against ID or civil register.

facts.fact: Newsmada reports that a UNDP tender this year covers servers and computers for CENI's management of biometric data, and that CENI received USD 750,000 of Japan-UNDP IT equipment on 23 October 2026 in preparation for a biometric voter list; the current overhaul still runs on an alphanumeric system, with over 7.16 million registered against a 14 million target.

Madagascar's electoral commission (Ceni) will collect voter data mainly on paper forms for the roll overhaul due in August 2026, with tablets in a limited number of centres only; the article says digitalisation is not yet in place.

note: Roll revision planned as an alphanumeric list with online registration among five modes; no digital or biometric register stated as procured, piloted or in service.

facts.fact: L'Express de Madagascar reports that the August 2026 overhaul of the voters' roll will rely mainly on paper voter information forms with tablets in only a few centres, and an electoral agent says no digitalisation is planned.

note: Only a statement that enrolment will end duplicates in electoral lists; no digital voter register is procured or piloted.
